selections.comment: A former bumper winner, the Gordon Elliott-trained WILLIAM BUTLER can register a first success over flights. Already placed twice from four starts over hurdles, the gelding has the experience to take a race of this nature. Fitted with first-time blinkers here, the five-year-old is likely to be ridden prominently around a tight track that suits such tactics. Having run his best race over hurdles to date when stepped up to this trip at Cork last time, the Philip Rothwell-trained Reiki Revolution should be a serious threat. A proven stayer, who had the speed to win a bumper, the Wings Of Eagles gelding won't be far away. Hurdling newcomer North Moon has to be respected for trainer Willie Mullins.

selections.comment: A couple of newcomners take the eye but ENAMORUS showed enough on debut in a class 2 maiden to suggest she can open her account sooner than later. She was well backed for her debut being sent off favourite and obviously is held in some regard by connections. This is a good opportunity to fulfill the promise. Ravishing, a No Nay Never filly costing 155,000 guineas looks the sort to make a splash on debut and is feared most hailing form the powerful Roger Varian yard who has been in fine form with his juveniles this term boasting close to a 33 per cwent strike-rate. Pacific Mission is another making her debut that could play a part but Princess Petrol is preferred and can make the frame having shown fair promise when not beaten too far on debut

selections.comment: A field bursting with potential with four defending unbeaten records in their brief careers. A BIT OF SPIRIT leads the way on form having built on a promising debut to scoot away in a decent novice last time upped to 7f. Clive Cox's colt is a smart prospect who has already shown a level of professionalism beyond his experience and can secure the hat-trick. Reciprocated is also seeking a hat-trick after two taking efforts landing a couple of decent novice events. Karl Burke's colt is big and showed a nice turn of foot last time to mow down the field and come away for a convincing four length win. The step up to 7f should suit and he'll be a tough nut to crack. Time To Turn, winner by ten lengths in a modest maiden last time after a couple of sound seconds, looks next best, just ahead of Tricky Tel, unbeaten and another hat-trick seeker, and the least experienced in the field and first time out winner Cape Ashizuri

selections.comment: A small but tight affair with CONTACTO just about setting the bar for last year's winning Andrew Balding stable. He was a nose behind Caprelo in the Northumberland Vase last time and, while a pound worse off, that was only his second start this term and first time on a synthetic surface. He's capable of better and can get back on an upward trajectory on just his tenth career start. Caprelo is a major danger again and while most of his form has been on the AW his turf form is just about on a par and he can push the selection hard. Many Men and Fireblade are admirably consistent sorts and both have sound claims but Blindedbythelights is feared a bit more. Sir Mark Prescott's charge has demonstrarted typical progression throughout his career and could have a bit more in the tank given this is only his fourth start since 2023. He flatenned out late first try over 2m last time but the winner that day is ultra-progressive and he merits another shot. He can play a big role

The former has been in tremendous form improving slightly last time in defeat after winning four of five runs prior. The race wsn't run to suit last time and granted a more solid pace the progression can continune. Dannick is interesting off te same mark as a good third last time where he was slightly tapped for toe in the quick ground after being short of room briefly. The juice in the ground should play to his strengths and he can go even closer. It's a tight call between War Howl, winner of a class 5 handicap last time and Arantes Nascimento who has repeatedly knocked on the door this term and should be suited by this stiffer track. The latter is just preferred

She's raced in the vanguard on both occassions so should have the pace to be handy enough but may prove vulnerable to LIL GUFF who arrives in top form and is capable of blazing a trail herself if need be but with Sugar Hill Babe in the field is likely to sit a bit behind before kicking into top gear late on. She could have a bit too much pace for the unbeaten Fantasy Obsessor. Sugar Hill Babe can hold on to take a share of the minor spoils ahead of Emeralds Pride

Whilst Quest For Fun is getting no younger, he has run well at this venue on two occasions; he can run well here and claim the 3rd place spot.

His runner here has won 3 out of her 11 career runs, which includes a win at Nottingham in June as well as two 2nds at Chester and Kempton, respectively. She has gone from a mark of 66 to start the season up to 73 currently, which looks like more than a workable mark for them going forward. She is running in the same class of contest as last time and looks the sort to go one better here in what is a bigger field than last time. Savrola was the Northumberland Vase winner last time out, and he is in cracking form at present. Winner of two races this season, as well as placing on his other two runs, he can go well and land another place in this contest behind a potentially well-treated rival. And It's All About You can continue where he left off with regard to his platform and run well to fill the places here.

That was a listed contest over the 7-furlong trip at Deauville, where she was a bit keen early on but ran with plenty of credit to claim 3rd spot and only get beaten by a little over 3 lengths in the end, with the race being won by an odds-on favourite. With this ease in class here, she can be seen to good effect in this and get off the mark at the third time of asking. Amakhala Warrior was a pretty nice debut winner over the 7-furlong trip at Haydock a few weeks back; he led towards the finish and held on nicely to win by a neck in the end. He can back that run up with a nicely placed effort here, whilst carrying the penalty. And Gold Dawn was a good 2nd on debut; he did disappoint last time out, but it is almost worth drawing a line through that effort. He can run well and claim a place spot here.

Noble Consort has been in brilliant form this season, with three wins and two places in just five career starts in 2025; he could go well once again and place in this contest for an in-form stable. And Alfa Whiteburd was a nice enough 2nd at this venue on his penultimate start; if he can build on that run, then he will place here once again.

selections.comment: RAINBOWS EDGE was in great form before her effort at Royal Ascot last time out; she was a well-fancied runner in the Kensington Palace Stakes, but she did hang right in the closing stages and did not really help her chances. However, she was a game enough winner at that venue beforehand, where she battled on gamely to land the prize by just under a length, getting a rise in the weights to 104 in the process. She runs off the same mark here as last time and tackles a listed company for the very first time. Connections hold her in high regard, and she looks the sort to progress nicely when tackling black-type races; this could be the perfect stepping stone for her at this stage in her career. Revoir is well regarded by her trainer and probably just found it all happening a bit too quickly for her in the Oaks last time; this step down in trip will suit her, and now back into Listed company, she can run well here. And Sand Gazelle did disappoint last time when in France; however, she did place at the Listed level at Newbury two starts ago; therefore, she can fill the places here.

Though she was defeated here earlier in the summer she still ran with credit and beat a field of in form rivals last time suggesting she had more in the tank. The biggest danger looks to be the similarly progressive Lady Roxby who has shown an excellent turn of foot in her short career. A 9lb rise for her latest victory is reasonable but she will need to prove her effectiveness on a softer surface here. The soft ground won't be an issue for the consistent and versatile Tiva so she is expected to complete the places.
